title: How search engines work
examples: How do search engines know what is on every website?
What is the difference between crawling and indexing?
Why are some search results better than others?

explain.say: A search engine needs to find websites first. This process is called crawling. A robot program does this work for us.

items: Search Engine Robot: Starts at a known page
Follows links: Moves from page to page
Discovers new content: Finds links to unknown sites

explain.say: The robot reads all the content it finds. It then sends this information to a big library system.
Indexing means organizing everything found. It creates a massive list of all the words and where they are.
When you search, the engine looks at its index. It finds all the pages that match your words quickly.

items: User types query: Search terms entered
Engine checks index: Finds matching pages
Algorithm scores pages: Determines best order

explain.say: The search engine then ranks the results. It decides which pages are most helpful for you to see first.
Think about finding a specific recipe online. The search engine crawls recipe sites, indexes the ingredients, and ranks the ones with the best reviews for you.

faq.q: Do search engines read every single word on the internet?
faq.a: No, they only read what they are programmed to crawl. They focus on important, accessible pages.
asks: How much of the web do they cover?

faq.q: Is the index the same as the search results?
faq.a: No, the index is the organized storage of information. The results are the final, ordered list shown to you.
asks: What is the difference between the index and the results?

faq.q: What makes one search result rank higher than another?
faq.a: The ranking uses complex rules to guess what is most trustworthy and useful. Factors like site quality are considered.
asks: How do they decide what is best?

faq.q: Does crawling happen all the time?
faq.a: Yes, search engines are constantly updating their knowledge. They crawl new and changed pages regularly.
asks: How often do they check websites?

faq.q: If I change a word on my website, do search engines know right away?
faq.a: Not immediately. The search engine must crawl the page again to notice the update. This takes time.
asks: Do I need to ask them to check?

facts: Crawling uses automated programs called spiders or bots.
Indexing stores keywords and their locations, not the whole page.
Ranking uses algorithms to determine relevance and authority.
Search engines cannot know everything instantly; they must visit pages.

quiz.say: A search engine robot moving from link to link is called:
quiz.why: Crawling is the first step where the robot discovers web pages.

wrong.0: Ranking is the final step of ordering the best results for the user.
wrong.1: Searching is the action the user takes, not the engine's process.
wrong.3: Indexing is the step where the discovered words are organized into a list.

quiz.say: If a search engine has already read a million pages, where does it store the keywords?
quiz.why: The index is the massive, organized database of all the content found.

wrong.0: The query is just the question you type in the search bar.
wrong.1: The rank is the final score, not the storage location of the words.
wrong.3: The web is the actual collection of pages, not the engine's storage.

quiz.say: When you search for 'best dogs for kids', the engine decides the order using:
quiz.why: Ranking is the process of scoring pages to show the most helpful ones first.

wrong.0: The query is just the input; it is not the deciding factor itself.
wrong.2: Crawling only finds the pages; it does not decide their order.
wrong.3: Indexing only organizes the words; it does not judge their quality.
